chunks: It was narrated to me by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Sa'dan ibn Muslim from Sulayman ibn Salih from his father from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
One who shoulders the coffin of a person, Allah will forgive his twenty-five greater sins; and if he shoulders it from all four sides, he will be released from sins.

key_terms.رَبَّعَ: He carried it from four sides / He was four

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for carrying a deceased person's coffin in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-A'mal*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes the immense spiritual merit of participating in funeral rites, specifically linking the physical act of carrying the coffin to the forgiveness of twenty-five major sins. The mention of 'rubba'a' (four sides) reflects the traditional Shia practice of four bearers, symbolizing communal support and the collective elevation of the deceased's status in the grave.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. It was narrated to me by Muhammad b. al-Hassan from Muhammad b. al-Hassan al-Saffar from al-Abbas b. Ma’ruf from Sa’dan b. Muslim from Sulayman b. Salih from his father from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said: “
One who shoulders the coffin of a person, Allah will forgive his twenty-five greater sins and one who shoulders the coffin from all four sides, Allah will purify him of his sins.”
